subject.title: fix(ollama): remote Ollama streaming stalls at model_call:started on slow hosts

question: Should native Ollama streams treat the configured request timeout as an idle no-progress timeout while chunks are arriving, matching sibling streaming transports, once remote-Ollama proof is supplied?
rationale: The code change is narrow and matches the shared guarded-fetch contract, but it deliberately changes the meaning of an existing provider timeout during streaming and the contributor has not yet proven the affected real setup.

options.title: Require proof, then accept idle semantics
options.body: Ask for redacted live output or logs from a remote or slow Ollama run, then merge if the refreshed branch remains clean.

options.title: Accept current unit proof
options.body: Maintainers can accept the compatibility change based on source and regression-test evidence, but the reported remote setup remains unproven.

options.title: Keep wall-clock timeout semantics
options.body: Reject this shape and ask for a different provider-owned fix that preserves timeoutSeconds as a total stream cap.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then accept idle semantics
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted live output or logs from a remote or slow Ollama run, then merge if the refreshed branch remains clean.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Ollama stream maintenance makes this the best available routing candidate for the timeout semantics decision.
